format model parameters in APA style

Source: R/anova.R, R/gam.R, R/lavaan.R, and 4 more
apa_parameters.Rd

format model parameters in APA style

Usage

# S3 method for class 'aov'
apa_parameters(
  fit,
  predictor_parameters = NULL,
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  t_with_df = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

model fit object

predictor_parameters

predictor parameters to display. If named vector, column names will be vector names. Columns not present in the model output (e.g., t for a model tested with z) are silently dropped. For lists of models, NULL (default) uses the default for each model's class. Add "CI" to show confidence intervals as [LL, UL] (headed, e.g., "95% CI"), and, for glm, polr, and clm models, "Exp_CI" to show confidence intervals of exponentiated coefficients (headed, e.g., "95% CI for OR"). Confidence intervals are not shown by default.

starred

columns to star with significant p_values

bolded

columns to bold, if significant

column_formats

column_formats object to format columns. If NULL, the default column_formats is used.

t_with_df

if TRUE, the t column will be displayed with degrees of freedom in parentheses. If FALSE, only the t value is displayed.

...

arguments passed to methods. For lm, glm, polr, and clm models, further arguments are passed to parameters::model_parameters(). For example, vcov = "HC3" gives heteroskedasticity-consistent (robust) standard errors, and the test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals are based on them. ci = .90 sets the confidence level.

exponentiate

if NULL (default), exponentiated coefficients are added when the model's link function is logit or log (i.e., odds ratios, risk ratios, or incidence rate ratios). If TRUE, exponentiated coefficients are always added. If FALSE, they are never added.

terms

for generalized additive models (mgcv::gam), which terms to show: "all" (default) for the parametric terms and the smooth terms under their own headings, "parametric", or "smooth"

standardize

for lavaan models, if TRUE (default), fully standardized estimates (\(\beta\)) are displayed with their standard errors and p-values. If FALSE, unstandardized estimates (B) are displayed.

variances, intercepts

for lavaan models, if TRUE, sections for (residual) variances or intercepts are added. Both are FALSE by default.

thresholds

for ordinal models, if TRUE (default), threshold (cutpoint) rows are displayed below the predictors. For lavaan models, if TRUE, a section for the thresholds of ordinal indicators is added (FALSE by default).

ci

for lavaan models, confidence level of intervals shown when predictor_parameters includes "CI"

groups

for multiple-group lavaan models, "columns" (default) shows the groups side by side, each under a column spanner, and "rows" stacks them, each under a heading row.

studies

for meta-analyses (metafor::rma()), if TRUE, the table has a row for each study (its effect size, confidence interval, and weight) followed by the pooled estimate. If FALSE, the table has the model's coefficients (the pooled estimate, or the intercept and moderators of a meta-regression). If NULL (default), TRUE for models without moderators and FALSE for meta-regressions.

weights

for the study rows of meta-analyses, if TRUE (default), each study's percentage of the total weight is shown

transform

for meta-analyses, if TRUE (default), effect sizes computed on a transformed scale are shown on their original scale: log risk ratios, odds ratios, incidence rate ratios, and ratios of means are exponentiated, and Fisher's z-transformed correlations are converted back to correlations. In meta-regressions, exponentiated coefficients are added in a separate column. If FALSE, estimates stay on the scale on which they were analyzed.

category_headings

for multinomial models, if TRUE (default), the coefficients of each outcome category are introduced by a heading row that names the comparison (e.g., "Part time vs. Not working"), with the predictors indented below it. If FALSE, each row is labeled with its category and predictor (e.g., "Part time: Children").

random

for mixed models, if TRUE (default), random-effect standard deviations and correlations (and the residual standard deviation, for linear mixed models) are displayed below the fixed effects.

effect_headings

for mixed models, if TRUE (default), the fixed and random effects are introduced by heading rows ("Fixed effects" and "Random effects"), with the effects indented below them. Headings are added only when random effects are displayed. The random-effects heading names the statistic of the SD (or variance) rows (e.g., "Random effects (SD)"), and each cluster (grouping factor) gets a subheading with its terms indented below it; correlation (or covariance) rows name their own statistic (e.g., "r (Constant, Days)"). Without headings, each random-effect label names its cluster and statistic (e.g., "Subject: SD (Days)").

random_scale

for mixed models, "sd" (default) displays random effects as standard deviations (SD) and correlations (r), and "variance" displays them as variances (Var) and covariances (Cov).

performance_parameters

for lists of models, model comparison metrics passed to apa_performance_comparison(). If NULL, no metrics are added. By default, R2 and deltaR2; for lists of mixed models (lme4), the default also includes the conditional R^2^ and its change (R2_conditional, deltaR2_conditional), and R2 is the marginal R^2^.

Value

tibble

Details

For aov models (including repeated-measures models with an Error() term) and afex models, apa_parameters() returns the ANOVA table from apa_anova(). predictor_parameters and t_with_df are ignored, and other arguments in ... (e.g., effect_size, type) are passed to apa_anova(). To display regression coefficients instead, refit the model with stats::lm().

For generalized additive models fit with mgcv::gam() or mgcv::bam(), the table has the parametric terms (coefficients, standard errors, and their t or z tests) and the smooth terms (effective degrees of freedom and their approximate F or \(\chi^2\) tests), as reported by summary(), under the headings "Parametric terms" and "Smooth terms". Smooth terms are labeled by their type and variables (e.g., "s(Age)" or "te(Longitude, Latitude)"), and smooths of a factor-by variable are labeled by level (e.g., "s(Age): Group = Treatment"). Coefficients of log and logit links are exponentiated by default, as for stats::glm() models. apa_note() names the method used to estimate the smoothing parameters.

For structural equation models and confirmatory factor analyses fit with lavaan, estimates come from lavaan::standardizedSolution() (standardize = TRUE, default) or lavaan::parameterEstimates() (standardize = FALSE). Each kind of parameter is introduced by a heading row: "Factor loadings" (e.g., Visual \(\rightarrow\) x1), "Regressions" (e.g., Speed \(\leftarrow\) Visual), "Correlations" (or "Covariances", if unstandardized; e.g., Visual \(\leftrightarrow\) Textual), and "Defined parameters" (e.g., indirect effects defined with :=), followed, if requested, by variances, intercepts, and thresholds. The default columns are the estimate, its standard error, and its p-value; "z", "CI", and (with standardize = TRUE) "Coefficient" for unstandardized estimates can be added to predictor_parameters. Unstandardized parameters fixed to set the scale of a factor (e.g., marker loadings fixed at 1) are not tested. Variable names are shown as written in the model, with the first letter capitalized and underscores replaced by spaces.

For multiple-group models (e.g., group = "school"), the groups are shown side by side by default, with one row for each parameter and a column spanner for each group, so that the groups can be compared row by row. With groups = "rows", each group has a heading row, with the kinds of parameters indented below it. A defined parameter that uses the labels of one group is shown with that group. One that combines groups (e.g., the difference between two groups' paths) is shown in the first group's columns, or under an "Across groups" heading. apa_note() gives the size of each group and names the parameters constrained to be equal across groups (group.equal), and any exceptions (group.partial). Standardized estimates of equal parameters can still differ across groups, because standardization uses each group's variances.

For meta-analyses fit with metafor::rma() (random-effects or equal-effects models, without or with moderators), the table of a model without moderators has a row for each study, labeled by the study labels (slab), with its effect size, confidence interval, and percentage of the total weight, followed by the pooled estimate under a rule. The column of effect sizes is named by the measure given to metafor::escalc() (e.g., g for standardized mean differences, r for correlations, and OR for odds ratios). apa_note() names the measure and the model (including the estimator of \(\tau^2\)), and gives the test of the pooled estimate, its prediction interval, and the test of heterogeneity. The table of a meta-regression has the intercept and moderators, as for other regression models. apa_performance() gives the heterogeneity statistics.

Multilevel meta-analyses fit with metafor::rma.mv() (e.g., several effect sizes nested in studies, with random = ~ 1 | study / effect) get the same tables, with a row for each effect size. apa_note() names the levels and their numbers of units, and gives each level's variance component (\(\sigma^2\)) and the multilevel \(I^2\) (Cheung, 2014). Random effects with an ~ inner | outer structure (e.g., correlated outcomes within studies) are not yet supported.

For multinomial logistic regression models (nnet::multinom), each outcome category except the reference category (the first level of the response) has its own block of coefficients, introduced by a heading row such as "Part time vs. Not working". Coefficients are log odds of the category relative to the reference category, tested with Wald z tests, and their exponentiated values (shown by default) are odds ratios relative to the reference category (sometimes called relative risk ratios), labeled OR. To compare the categories with a different reference, relevel the response (e.g., with stats::relevel()) before fitting the model. apa_note() names the reference category.

For zero-inflated and hurdle count models fit with pscl::zeroinfl() and pscl::hurdle(), the count model and the zero model are each introduced by a heading row ("Count model" and "Zero-inflation model" or "Zero hurdle model"). Coefficients are tested with Wald z tests. Only the count model's coefficients are exponentiated (by default), giving incidence rate ratios (IRR), because the zero model has a different link and meaning. In a zero-inflated model, the zero model predicts excess zeros (zeros not produced by the count model); in a hurdle model, it predicts whether the count is greater than zero. apa_note() says which, names the count distribution, and gives the negative binomial dispersion parameter (\(\theta\)).

For glm objects (including MASS::glm.nb), the test statistic is z for families with a fixed dispersion parameter (binomial, Poisson, negative binomial) and t for families with an estimated dispersion parameter (Gaussian, Gamma, inverse Gaussian, quasi families). Whichever statistic applies is displayed. The exponentiated coefficient column (Exp_Coefficient) is labeled OR for logit links, IRR for log links in count models (Poisson, quasi-Poisson, negative binomial), RR for log links in binomial models, and Exp(B) otherwise.

For ordinal regression models (MASS::polr and ordinal::clm), coefficients are tested with Wald z tests. (parameters reports t for polr, but the test is asymptotically normal, and clm reports z for the same model.) With a logit link, exponentiated coefficients are cumulative odds ratios, labeled OR. Threshold rows show only the estimate, its standard error, and its confidence interval, because their exponentiated values are not odds ratios, and testing whether a threshold equals 0 is not meaningful. Confidence intervals ("CI", "Exp_CI") are Wald z intervals, consistent with the z tests.

For mixed models fit with lme4 (lmer and glmer), fixed effects are displayed as for lm and glm models. For linear mixed models, t tests and confidence intervals use Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom by default (ci_method = "kenward", which requires the pbkrtest package); pass another ci_method (e.g., "satterthwaite", which requires lmerTest, or "wald") to change this. When the degrees of freedom differ across fixed effects, they are shown in a df column rather than in the t column header. Random-effect rows show only the estimated standard deviation (SD) or correlation (r), or with random_scale = "variance", the variance (Var) or covariance (Cov), grouped by cluster (grouping factor) under a subheading for each cluster, with nested clusters named, e.g., "Classroom in School". The fixed and random effects are introduced by heading rows (effect_headings = TRUE). The random-effects heading names the statistic of the SD or variance rows (e.g., "Random effects (SD)"), and correlation or covariance rows name their own (e.g., "r (Constant, Days)"). apa_note() defines the symbols.

For mixed models fit with glmmTMB::glmmTMB(), fixed effects are tested with z tests, and random effects are displayed as for lme4 models. Coefficients of log and logit links are exponentiated by default (e.g., IRR for Poisson and negative binomial models). When the model has a zero-inflation part (ziformula) or a dispersion part (dispformula), each part is introduced by a heading row ("Conditional model", "Zero-inflation model", or "Dispersion model"), and only the conditional model's coefficients are exponentiated. A dispersion parameter that is not modeled (i.e., without a dispformula) is not displayed.

For linear mixed models fit with nlme::lme(), fixed effects are tested with t tests whose degrees of freedom are computed by nlme from the grouping levels at which each effect varies, and random effects are displayed as for lme4 models. Parameters of residual correlation structures (correlation, e.g., nlme::corAR1()) and variance functions (weights, e.g., nlme::varIdent()) are displayed below the residual SD, and apa_note() names the structures.

References

Cheung, M. W.-L. (2014). Modeling dependent effect sizes with three-level meta-analyses: A structural equation modeling approach. Psychological Methods, 19(2), 211–229. doi:10.1037/a0032968

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE)) {
  mgcv::gam(mpg ~ am + s(hp, k = 5) + s(wt, k = 5), data = mtcars,
            method = "REML") |>
    apa_parameters()
}
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   Variable         `*B*`   `*SE*` `*t*(25.43)` `*edf*` `*F*`  `*p*`  
#>   <chr>            <chr>   <chr>  <chr>        <chr>   <chr>  <chr>  
#> 1 Parametric terms ""      ""     ""           ""      ""     ""     
#> 2  Constant        "19.86" "0.69" "28.67"      ""      ""     "<.001"
#> 3  Am              " 0.57" "1.43" " 0.40"      ""      ""     " .70 "
#> 4 Smooth terms     ""      ""     ""           ""      ""     ""     
#> 5  s(Hp)           ""      ""     ""           "2.36"  "5.46" " .006"
#> 6  s(Wt)           ""      ""     ""           "2.21"  "5.83" " .005"
# }
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)) {
  model <- "visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
            textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
            speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9
            speed ~ visual + textual"
  lavaan::sem(model, data = lavaan::HolzingerSwineford1939) |>
    apa_parameters()

  # Multiple groups, side by side
  lavaan::cfa(
    "visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3",
    data = lavaan::HolzingerSwineford1939,
    group = "school",
    group.equal = "loadings"
  ) |>
    apa_parameters()
}
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   Parameter   `Pasteur_&beta;` `Pasteur_*SE*` `Pasteur_*p*` `Grant-White_&beta;`
#>   <chr>       <chr>            <chr>          <chr>         <chr>               
#> 1 Factor loa… ""               ""             ""            ""                  
#> 2  Visual → … ".61"            "0.07"         "<.001"       ".60"               
#> 3  Visual → … ".48"            "0.07"         "<.001"       ".52"               
#> 4  Visual → … ".72"            "0.08"         "<.001"       ".77"               
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: `Grant-White_*SE*` <chr>, `Grant-White_*p*` <chr>
# }
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d_bcg <- metafor::escalc(
    measure = "RR",
    ai = tpos, bi = tneg, ci = cpos, di = cneg,
    data = metadat::dat.bcg,
    slab = paste(author, year)
  )
  fit_meta <- metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = d_bcg)
  apa_parameters(fit_meta)
  apa_performance(fit_meta)

  # Meta-regression
  metafor::rma(yi, vi, mods = ~ ablat, data = d_bcg) |>
    apa_parameters()
}
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   Variable `*B*` `*SE*` `95% CI`       `*RR*` `*z*` `*p*`
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>  <chr>          <chr>  <chr> <chr>
#> 1 Constant  0.25 0.25   [−0.24,  0.74] 1.29    1.01  .31 
#> 2 Ablat    −0.03 0.01   [−0.04, −0.01] 0.97   −4.04 <.001
# }
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("nnet", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("carData", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d <- carData::Womenlf
  d$partic <- relevel(d$partic, ref = "not.work")
  nnet::multinom(partic ~ hincome + children, data = d, trace = FALSE) |>
    apa_parameters()
}

# Confidence intervals with robust (HC3) standard errors
if (requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)) {
  lm(mpg ~ cyl + wt, data = mtcars) |>
    apa_parameters(
      predictor_parameters = c("Parameter", "Coefficient", "SE", "CI", "t", "df_error", "p"),
      vcov = "HC3"
    ) |>
    apa_flextable()
}
